title: ABM Landing Page Copy Draft — Healthcare (Regulated Workloads / PHI)
content:
Working draft for Healthcare ABM landing page.
Owner: PMM (Soojin). Growth (Ben) will adapt for final layout + form + UTMs.

Notes / guardrails (please don’t “polish away”):
- We should not imply “HIPAA certified” or that a customer is automatically compliant by using Redwood.
- Keep PHI-safe messaging: emphasize deployment boundaries, logging/retention controls, auditability, and customer control.
- Avoid absolute claims like “we never store prompts/outputs” without tying to deployment mode + configured retention. Point to Security FAQ addendum.
- CTA should bias toward a security + architecture session, not a generic “contact sales.”

============================================================
PAGE GOAL
============================================================
Primary conversion: schedule a 30–45 min Security + Architecture session (CISO/GRC + Platform/ML).
Secondary conversion: request the Healthcare Security FAQ addendum (gated) and/or ask for a Private/VPC reference architecture walkthrough.

============================================================
HERO (headline + subhead + proof + CTA)
============================================================
Headline options (pick 1):
A) "LLM inference for healthcare workloads—without compromising PHI boundaries"
B) "Run clinical AI features with predictable performance and deployment control"
C) "Production-grade LLM inference for regulated healthcare data"

Subhead options (pick 1):
A) "Redwood Inference helps healthcare teams ship patient-facing and clinician-facing AI features with low latency, cost control, and deployment models designed for regulated environments—including Private deployments in your VPC or on-prem."
B) "From hosted pilots to Private/VPC deployments, Redwood delivers a consistent inference runtime with the operational controls security teams expect: auditability, retention controls, and customer-managed key integration options."

Supporting bullets (3–5):
- "Choose the right boundary: Hosted → Dedicated → Private (VPC/on-prem)"
- "Predictable latency & throughput for production endpoints"
- "Audit-friendly controls: logs, access controls, and export paths to your systems"
- "Data residency & retention options (by region + deployment mode)"

Primary CTA button copy (pick 1):
- "Schedule a PHI readiness review"
- "Book a security & architecture session"
- "Talk to a regulated-workloads SE"

Secondary CTA (text link):
- "Get the Healthcare security FAQ" (gated PDF / email follow-up)
- "See the Private/VPC reference architecture" (docs link; still okay if it’s high-level)

Hero microcopy (under CTA):
"We’ll align on data boundaries, retention, audit logging needs, and a safe evaluation plan."

============================================================
WHO THIS IS FOR (quick qualification)
============================================================
Section title options:
- "Built for teams that can’t treat PHI like test data"
- "When security reviews are on the critical path"

Copy:
"If your AI roadmap includes PHI, regulated clinical data, or strict audit requirements, the inference layer can’t be a black box. Redwood is designed for teams that need production-grade performance and a deployment story security teams can approve."

Example scenarios (bullets):
- "Clinical note summarization and chart review copilots"
- "Patient communications review and call center assist"
- "Clinical search, coding support, and prior auth workflows"
- "Operational analytics where logs and access must be auditable"

============================================================
CORE VALUE PROP (3 pillars)
============================================================
Section title: "Performance you can measure. Controls you can explain."

Pillar 1: Predictable performance
- "Low-latency inference for interactive clinician workflows"
- "Throughput planning for peak-hour demand"
- "Operational visibility into latency and error modes"

Pillar 2: Deployment control for regulated data
- "Start fast with Hosted for non-PHI workloads or early prototyping"
- "Move to Dedicated for predictable capacity and isolation"
- "Use Private (VPC/on-prem) when PHI boundaries require it"

Pillar 3: Auditability and operational tooling
- "Audit log and event export paths for your security tooling (SIEM-ready patterns)"
- "Role-based access controls and SSO posture (details in Security FAQ)"
- "Retention/residency options aligned to your policy (details depend on deployment)"

(Inline disclaimer, small text):
"Security and compliance requirements vary by organization. Redwood supports common controls and deployment patterns; we’ll map them to your policies during review."

============================================================
DEPLOYMENT MODEL DECISION TREE (key section)
============================================================
Section title options:
- "Pick the right deployment boundary for PHI"
- "Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private: which one fits your data?"

Intro copy:
"Most healthcare teams don’t start with on-prem on day one—but most also can’t accept unknown data handling in production. Redwood supports a practical path from evaluation to regulated deployment without changing your API surface."

Decision tree (layout as a simple flow):

1) "Are you processing PHI (or data classified equivalent to PHI) in prompts/outputs?"
- If NO → "Hosted API or Dedicated" (continue to #2)
- If YES → "Private (VPC or on-prem)" (jump to Private summary)

2) "Do you need guaranteed capacity and tenant isolation for production SLOs?"
- If NO → "Hosted API" (summary)
- If YES → "Dedicated" (summary)

3) "Do you require customer-managed networking and explicit control of data plane boundaries (VPC / on-prem)?"
- If YES → "Private" (summary)

Deployment summaries (each with 2–4 bullets):

Hosted API (fastest start)
- "Best for prototyping, dev/test, and non-PHI workloads"
- "Simple API + console observability"
- "Security posture documented; ask for the Healthcare Security FAQ"

Dedicated (predictable capacity)
- "Reserved capacity for consistent throughput and isolation"
- "Recommended for production workloads with tight SLOs"
- "Clear path to Private if/when data boundary requirements change"

Private (VPC / on-prem) (strongest boundary)
- "Designed for regulated workloads where PHI must remain within your controlled environment"
- "Customer-managed networking (VPC) and integration points for customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM options)"
- "Audit-friendly architecture patterns, including export to your logging/SIEM stack"

Decision tree microcopy (important):
"If there’s any uncertainty about PHI classification, we recommend starting with a security + architecture session before running a production evaluation."

============================================================
REFERENCE ARCHITECTURE TEASER (Private / VPC)
============================================================
Section title: "A Private deployment architecture your security team can review"

Copy:
"Redwood Private is designed to fit into healthcare security programs: clear network boundaries, explicit integration points, and an operational model that defines responsibilities (Redwood vs. your team)."

Bullets (keep high level; details in doc):
- "Network boundary: Private control plane + customer-managed VPC connectivity"
- "Key management: integration points for customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM)"
- "Audit pipeline: patterns to export audit events/logs to your SIEM"
- "Operational clarity: roles, patching model, and change control overview"

CTA (secondary):
- "Request the reference architecture" OR "Walk through the architecture with an SE"

============================================================
SECURITY / COMPLIANCE SECTION (PHI-safe language)
============================================================
Section title options:
- "Security teams ask the same questions—here are the answers"
- "Controls and evidence for regulated evaluations"

Copy (keep non-absolute, questionnaire-friendly):
"Security reviews are a normal part of regulated healthcare deployments. Redwood provides documented security controls and standard evidence packages under NDA where appropriate. We’ll align on data handling assumptions, retention requirements, audit logging expectations, and residency needs before you run a PHI-adjacent evaluation."

Checklist bullets (exact items may shift based on Security’s final wording):
- "Audit logging: what events are captured and how exports work"
- "Retention: configurable policies and what is/ isn’t retained (by deployment mode)"
- "Encryption: in transit and at rest; key management integration options"
- "Access controls: SSO/RBAC posture and administrative actions auditability"
- "Residency: region options and how to meet data localization policies"

CTA: "Get the Healthcare Security FAQ" (gated)
Microcopy: "Ideal for CISO/GRC review; includes questionnaire-ready language."

============================================================
USE CASES (healthcare-specific, concrete)
============================================================
Section title: "Common healthcare workflows we support"

Use case tiles (copy per tile):
1) Clinical summarization
"Generate structured summaries from clinician notes with low latency and consistent output formats."

2) Chart review assistant
"Enable rapid retrieval + synthesis across patient context while controlling deployment boundaries."

3) Patient communications review
"Assist with message drafting and review workflows, with auditability for policy and safety reviews."

4) Prior auth / coding support
"Accelerate administrative workflows with predictable throughput and cost controls."

Optional line:
"Need a specific model, context window, or routing policy? We’ll scope this in the architecture session."

============================================================
OBJECTIONS / FAQ (short, safe)
============================================================
FAQ intro:
"Below are fast answers. For detailed, evidence-backed responses, request the Healthcare Security FAQ addendum."

Q1: "Can we use Redwood with PHI?"
A: "Many healthcare teams require strict PHI boundaries. For PHI workloads, Redwood typically recommends Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) so data plane boundaries align with your security policy. We’ll confirm requirements in a PHI readiness review."

Q2: "Do you store prompts or outputs?"
A: "Data handling depends on deployment mode and configuration (including retention settings and logging choices). We’ll walk through the specifics and provide approved written language in the Healthcare Security FAQ."

Q3: "Can we control where data is processed?"
A: "Yes—residency options vary by deployment and region. We’ll map your residency policy to an approved deployment plan."

Q4: "How do audit logs work?"
A: "Redwood supports audit-friendly patterns, including export paths to your security tooling. The FAQ includes details on log types, retention, and export options."

Q5: "What’s the path from evaluation to production?"
A: "Start with a short security + architecture session, run a scoped evaluation with success criteria (latency/throughput/cost), then align on security review milestones and procurement steps."

============================================================
FINAL CTA (bottom of page)
============================================================
Headline options:
- "Get a PHI-safe deployment plan in 30 minutes"
- "Schedule a security & architecture session"

CTA module copy:
"Bring your CISO/GRC and platform lead. We’ll leave you with: (1) a recommended deployment model, (2) data boundary assumptions, (3) a short evidence checklist for your security questionnaire, and (4) a scoped evaluation plan."

Primary CTA button:
"Book a security & architecture session"

Secondary CTA:
"Request the Healthcare Security FAQ"

Trust microcopy (small):
"We can share additional evidence under NDA as needed."

============================================================
FORM COPY (for scheduling / routing)
============================================================
Form title:
"Schedule a PHI readiness review"

Form helper text:
"Tell us what you’re building and your deployment constraints. We’ll route you to a regulated-workloads SE and Security/GRC support as needed."

Suggested fields (Growth Ops to implement):
- Work email
- Company
- Role (dropdown): Security/GRC, Platform Eng, ML Eng, Product, Other
- Use case (dropdown): clinical summarization, chart review, comms review, prior auth/coding, other
- Data classification (dropdown): no PHI, PHI possible, PHI confirmed
- Desired deployment (dropdown): hosted, dedicated, private VPC, on-prem, not sure
- Residency requirement (free text)
- Anything your security team is asking for right now? (free text)

Submit button:
"Schedule review"

Post-submit confirmation:
"Thanks—someone will reach out within 1 business day to schedule. If you have a security questionnaire or required controls list, you can reply with it to speed up review."

============================================================
INTERNAL NOTES / OPEN QUESTIONS
============================================================
1) Security phrasing:
- Waiting on final approved language for the retention/prompts/outputs answer (must align with the Healthcare Security FAQ addendum).

2) On-prem messaging:
- Keep “on-prem option” as available but avoid implying same-day install. If asked, route to SE.

3) Proof points:
- Do we want to add a small “What teams measure” box (latency p95, throughput, cost/token, audit events captured)? Might help platform buyers.

4) SEO/meta (Ben to handle):
- Proposed page title: "Healthcare LLM Inference (PHI-Safe Deployments) | Redwood Inference"
- Proposed H1: whichever hero headline we pick.

5) CTA routing:
- If form indicates “PHI confirmed” + “Private/on-prem” → auto-route to Markus Klein / Fatima Noor + notify Security FAQ owner (Kevin Osei) for evidence.

End.
